video.title: Charlotte Hornets 2026/27 Season: Ultimate Preview & Insider Secrets!

summary: Josh Lloyd talks with Walker Mehl of Locked On Hornets to preview the Charlotte Hornets after a big offseason. Charlotte traded LaMelo Ball to Minnesota and Miles Bridges away. They brought in Naz Reid, Royce O'Neale, Grayson Allen and Dorian Finney-Smith, drafted Hunter Steinbach and Christian Anderson, and re-signed Coby White to start at point guard. The projected starters are Coby White, Kon Knueppel, Brandon Miller, Naz Reid and Moussa Diabaté. Steinbach is expected to be the next big man and Ryan Kalkbrenner the last. The team will lean further into shooting threes, steals and offensive rebounds, and playmaking will come from several players instead of one. Walker predicts 43 wins and names Coby White as the player who sets the team's ceiling. Josh adds that lottery reform should push up win totals at the bottom of the league.

rules.text: When a team is out of contention, games a player misses with injuries can look worse than they are. On a good team, the same player may play through those injuries.
rules.quote: when this team is good he'll play through them and yeah, that's what happened

rules.text: With lottery reform, fewer teams will finish with very low win totals. Wins shift away from the middle and top teams, so expect win projections to bunch closer together.
rules.quote: with the lottery reform system, there's not going to be four teams that finish under 25

rules.text: Bad teams that used to win about 17 games may now win about 24, because they will play their regular players late in the season.
rules.quote: These bad 17 win teams might be 24 win teams.

rules.text: When a player has an outlier shooting season on high volume, expect the volume to come back down toward his career norm.
rules.quote: Grayson, the outlier shooting year for him, just happened this past season and the volume's going to come back down

player_notes.text: He was traded from Charlotte to Minnesota.
player_notes.quote: the lack of play making that you'll be missing with LaMelo playing basketball up in Minnesota

player_notes.text: He is one of the best passers and transition players in the NBA.
player_notes.quote: he is one of the best passers in the NBA, one of the best transition players in the NBA

player_notes.text: He had a usage rate over 30 percent and piled up assists.
player_notes.quote: Ball had a 30 plus usage. He was assisting like crazy.

player_notes.text: He has a long history of ankle injuries, including impingement.
player_notes.quote: But he has a ton of ankle injuries, man. Like he's got impingement.

player_notes.text: Finishing at the rim has been his biggest weakness, and he does not get to the free throw line much.
player_notes.quote: rim finishing LaMelo that was probably his biggest weakness throughout his entire NBA career to this point

player_notes.text: Last season Charlotte held him to a 27-minute restriction and saved his minutes for fourth quarters.
player_notes.quote: playing him in the fourth quarter to maximize him and not go a second over that 27-minute restriction

player_notes.text: He gets into the paint more than LaMelo Ball did, finishes at the rim and gets to the free throw line more.
player_notes.quote: LaMelo and can also finish at the rim and get to the foul line more than LaMelo

player_notes.text: He is the projected starting point guard. Walker expects his minutes to rise from about 19 per game to about 30, because the team has no backup point guard he trusts.
player_notes.quote: once we up that 19 minute per game average according to Cleaning the Glass to like 30

player_notes.text: He is a fine passer, but the offense cannot be built around his vision the way it was around LaMelo Ball.
player_notes.quote: Now, Kobe White is not known to be a good passer. He is a fine passer

player_notes.text: He has a big enough sample now to count as a good shooter, including off the dribble.
player_notes.quote: I think we have enough sample on Kobe being a good shooter now, especially off of the dribble as well.

player_notes.text: His usage is already high, and his assist usage has risen to about average. Walker names him as the player who sets the team's ceiling because he will have the ball so much.
player_notes.quote: The assist usage percentage has gone up to where it's about average.

player_notes.text: He has been more durable than LaMelo Ball over the last four years, despite some injuries last season.
player_notes.quote: while also being a more durable basketball player even with some injuries that he had to go through last season

player_notes.text: He came over in the LaMelo Ball trade and is projected to start at power forward in place of Miles Bridges. He is a very good floor spacer who brings physicality.
player_notes.quote: you replace Miles with Naz Reid who was a very good floor spacer and brings physicality

player_notes.text: His rebounding and defense have improved compared with earlier in his career.
player_notes.quote: also a little bit better rebounding than I think what he showed early in his career

player_notes.text: People who covered him think he could become a fringe All-Star in a bigger role. Walker expects him and Diabaté to play the most frontcourt minutes.
player_notes.quote: in an increased role maybe he can be a fringe All-Star

player_notes.text: Walker expects him to start at center on opening night.
player_notes.quote: I think all of those things culminate into Moussa starting game one of the NBA season.

player_notes.text: He was one of the best offensive rebounders in the league last season. He gets steals, switches onto ball handlers and is improving as a passer on short rolls.
player_notes.quote: because Moussa was one of the best offensive rebounders in the game last year

player_notes.text: After Gordon Hayward got hurt, Diabaté played about 28 minutes a game, and Charlotte had the top offensive rating and the fifth-best defensive rating in that stretch. He won Hustle Player of the Year.
player_notes.quote: they have the number one offensive rating, the fifth best defensive rating, which is the real shocker here

player_notes.text: He was the best rebounder in college basketball, and that carried over to Summer League. He can shoot a little.
player_notes.quote: Steinbach was the best rebounder in all of college basketball.

player_notes.text: He is expected to be next in the frontcourt rotation after Diabaté and Reid. He can play alongside Diabaté in four-out lineups, and some people are talking about starting him.
player_notes.quote: I would say Musa, Naz, those guys are getting the most minutes. I would say Steinbach is next

player_notes.text: He was very efficient when he started. The team did not let him shoot from the perimeter. He is the best rim protector among Charlotte's bigs.
player_notes.quote: which by the way, they didn't let Kolbrenner shoot. Not a great shooter at Creighton

player_notes.text: He is expected to be last in the center rotation.
player_notes.quote: I do think he's at the very end of the center rotation that we're discussing right now.

player_notes.text: Walker expects Knueppel to take on more of the creation load than Brandon Miller. He calls Knueppel a good passer.
player_notes.quote: Kankan and Brandon, I think Kankan is a good passer.

player_notes.text: His drives often stall, which leads to many mid-range shots. He finishes well at the rim but rarely gets there, partly because he is injured so often.
player_notes.quote: He shoots pretty well at the cup. He just doesn't get there at all.

player_notes.text: His shooting volume should drop from last season's outlier level. Walker expects higher efficiency, and Allen should help as a secondary creator off the bench.
player_notes.quote: Grayson, the outlier shooting year for him, just happened this past season and the volume's going to come back down

player_notes.text: He hit corner threes all season long.
player_notes.quote: Royce was just banging corner threes all season long.

player_notes.text: His finishing at the rim declined as he got older. His three-point shot was never there outside one outlier season.
player_notes.quote: the finishing at the rim started to dwindle for Miles as he got older

player_notes.text: His on-ball minutes have not gone well.
player_notes.quote: Seon James on-ball minutes, they've not gone well at all.

player_notes.text: The 18th overall pick is not yet trusted as the backup point guard. Walker calls him a fun archetype rather than a functional one for now.
player_notes.quote: it's more so a fun archetype than it is a functional one right now

team_notes.text: The team is leaning fully into spacing the floor and will take a lot of threes.
team_notes.quote: way into spacing the floor out and they're going to take a ton of threes

team_notes.text: The team also emphasizes steals and offensive rebounds.
team_notes.quote: I think the other thing they're emphasizing is stealing possessions and grabbing a whole bunch a bunch of offensive rebounds

team_notes.text: There is no trusted backup point guard on the roster.
team_notes.quote: we don't really have a backup point guard that I trust right now on the roster

team_notes.text: Playmaking is expected to be spread across several players instead of one primary creator.
team_notes.quote: I do think that a lot of the play making is going to come in the aggregate

team_notes.text: Coach Charles Lee is expected to experiment with frontcourt lineups. Starters should stay stable, but closing lineups will vary by matchup.
team_notes.quote: the starting lineup will probably be the same cuz you don't want to tinker with that too much

team_notes.text: Charlotte has a $40 million trade exception and could add a player at the deadline.
team_notes.quote: Are you going to use the trade exception? It's worth $40 million. It's the biggest in NBA history.

team_notes.text: Walker predicts 43 wins and says the team is deeper than last year.
team_notes.quote: So I'm going with 43 victories and maybe it serves as symbolism
